newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Fernandez explains Brazil trip delay.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Fernandez explains Brazil trip delay.

text.p: Argentina's Economy Minister Roque Fernandez announced Monday he was postponing his planned trip to Brazil to argue against new Brazilian import rules that would hurt Argentine exports.

"I am sorry I have to announce this, but my presence in Brazil will not be justified until we see that we can truly make progress on a negotiation within the framework of Mercosur", Fernandez told reporters. Fernandez said two of his top aides would travel to Brazil on Tuesday to begin talks and he would go himself on Wednesday only if conditions for "constructive negotiations" were met.

Brazil's Central Bank, trying to slim a growing trade deficit, ruled that most Brazilian importers with financing of less than 360 days will have to take out foreign exchange contracts on the day they receive their goods from customs.
Argentina, which posted a $1 billion trade surplus exporting goods worth $6.5 billion to its neighbour in 1996, wants Brazil to exclude its Mercosur customs union partners.
Mercosur also groups Uruguay and Paraguay, while Chile is an associate member. All of Brazil's regional partners have complained about the new rules.
Fernandez said he was worried about the "protectionist spirit" of large sections of the Brazilian media who wholeheartedly backed the new measures.
"This is not the message we got from the Brazilian government," said Fernandez.
He added that, if "Mecosur prevails", he hopes in the future there will be a formal system of consultation so prevent trade problems from coming "as a surprise."
